overview: A chain of Pacific systems keeps the West snowy this week, with a strong storm Saturday in the northern Rockies and Sierra and a series of weaker ones after that. The Northeast gets rain first, then a wetter-than-usual Saturday night.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Grand Targhee is forecast for about 36". Jackson Hole and Big Sky follow. Winter Storm Warning at Grand Targhee from Friday to Saturday.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Brighton is forecast for about 26". Solitude and Alta follow.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Sunday brings the first of several systems to the Sierra, with rain below about 8,000 feet and snow above. Gusts can reach 80 mph on the ridges. Kirkwood leads the region with 27 inches for the week, 10 of them Monday. Snow levels fall further Tuesday into Wednesday.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Mt. Bachelor is forecast for about 28". Mt. Baker and Crystal Mountain follow. The National Weather Service has rain mixed in at Mt. Baker Monday and Monday night.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Jay Peak is forecast for about 25". Mont-Sainte-Anne and Whiteface follow. Environment Canada has rain mixed in at Mont-Sainte-Anne Friday night.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Steamboat is forecast for about 21", 18" of it Saturday. Vail and Breckenridge follow. Winter Storm Warning at Steamboat from Friday to Sunday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: A mild, wet pattern holds for the coast, with rain on most days. Cypress Mountain leads with 18 inches for the week, 7 of them Monday, and Whistler has 13.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Gusty winds of 55 to 65 mph hit the Sierra Friday night into Saturday morning, then a stronger storm arrives Sunday. Snow falls above about 7,000 feet by Monday, and Mammoth leads with 14 inches for the week. The National Weather Service says snowfall rises to 12 to 24 inches from Sunday night through Tuesday night.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Mixed rain and snow with frequent flurries through the week. Whitewater leads with 12 inches for the week, 6 of them Monday, and Fernie has 11. Snow levels stay low enough that most of the snow falls at the mountain tops.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Sun Peaks is forecast for about 7", 4" of it Monday. Big White and SilverStar follow. Environment Canada has rain mixed in at Big White Monday.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Snow and blowing snow hit the central Colorado mountains through Saturday night. Winds of 55 to 65 mph follow a strong front across the eastern plains Saturday. Wolf Creek leads with 6 inches for the week, all of it Wednesday. The National Weather Service says the next storm brings 6 to 13 inches Tuesday night through Wednesday night.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
